children: WINNIPEG, Manitoba--Canola futures on the Intercontinental Exchange were in positive territory on Thursday, following the lead of comparable oils.

Crude oil prices surged by more than US$3 per barrel after Houthi rebels attacked King Khalid Airport in Riyadh on consecutive days. United States President Donald Trump said today he had productive talks with Iran and will not attack the country before midterm elections.
Chicago soyoil, European rapeseed and Malaysian palm oil were higher as well.
Saskatchewan's canola harvest progressed 27 points and was 72 per cent finished on Oct. 5.
At mid-afternoon, the Canadian dollar was up more than one-tenth of a U.S. cent compared to Wednesday's close.
There were 97,978 canola contracts traded on Thursday, compared to Wednesday when 97,099 contracts changed hands. Spreads accounted for 61,482 contracts in today's trade.
Settlement prices are in Canadian dollars per metric tonne.
